title: Replace All ?'s to Avoid Consecutive Repeating Characters
summary: Given a string s with lowercase letters and '?' characters, replace each '?' with a lowercase letter to ensure no two consecutive characters are the same.
statement: Given a string s with lowercase letters and '?' characters, replace each '?' with a lowercase letter to ensure no two consecutive characters are the same. Non '?' characters remain unchanged. Ensure no consecutive repeating characters exist in the final string. Return any valid string if multiple solutions exist.
constraints: Replace every question mark while leaving other lowercase letters unchanged and avoiding equal adjacent characters.
For deterministic practice, return the lexicographically smallest valid result.
hints: Only the left replacement and immediate right original character can constrain the current question mark.
Try a, b, then c and choose the first differing from both neighbors.
Three letters guarantee at least one choice.
Greedy lexical choice is safe because later positions depend only on the chosen current character and still retain at least two alternatives.
editorial: Greedy lexical choice is safe because later positions depend only on the chosen current character and still retain at least two alternatives.

tests.explanation: Choosing a is valid and lexicographically smallest, producing azs.
The smallest choice different from v and w is a, producing ubvaw.
